newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to be top LatAm ADR issuer within yr-Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to be top LatAm ADR issuer within yr-Morgan.

text.p: Brazil is likely to become Latin America's top issuer of American Depositary Receipts (ADR) in the next 12 months, surpassing Mexico and Argentina, U.S. investment bank J.P. Morgan said.
"The power and size of deals from Brazil coming to the market this year will outrank any other country in Latin America," bank Vice President Eduard van Raay told Reuters.
"There's a high likelihood that in a year Brazil will rank No. 1 in the region," he added.
Boasting Latin America's largest economy, Brazil nonetheless remains under-represented in U.S. equity markets, ranking third after Mexico and Argentina in value of ADR programs.
But Brazilian firms, which now account for $10 billion in issued and outstanding shares, are expected to issue roughly $3.5 billion more in ADRs in the next 12 months, van Raay said.
"It's very hard to project but you can look at the companies coming to market -- Petrobras, Odebrecht to $4 billion," he said.

In September 1996, there were 36 Brazilian ADR programs, second among Latin American countries after Mexico's 60 programs but well ahead of Argentina, Chile and Colombia, "but only five (of the programs) are of any real size."
Only one Brazilian firm -- Telecomunicacoes Brasileiras S.A. (Telebras) -- is among the 11 largest Latin American ADRs that account for 75 percent of the total in value from the region.
"The disparity between Brazil and the other Latin American countries is the fact that you have so few listed companies," Van Raay said.
That is about to change. Just two local companies are now listed on the New York Stock Exchange -- federal telecoms giant Telebras and private paper and pulp firm Aracruz Celulose S.A..
But they are likely to be joined this year by beer and soda pop maker Brahma, Minas Gerais state power firm (CSN), van Raay said.
Federal power holding Eletrobras and state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) are expected to be listed in 1998, he said.

Power firm Light is also preparing for a New York listing, he added. Eletrobras, CVRD and Cemig already trade in the United States as level one ADRs but do not yet have approval for a level three program to list on the Big Board.
Appreciation in Brazilian shares, particularly bellwether Telebras, since September also accounts for the country's rise in terms of value in the ranking of Latin American ADR issuers.
Telebras has jumped by 30 percent from $70 per ADR six months ago to $100 per ADR today and market analysts expect it will continue climbing this year as the company is broken up and privatized.
